To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the protective antibody titers were higher in sheep reared in experimental condition than those reared in village condition.
sheep reared under good managemental practices with booster vaccination of E. coli vaccine showed better immune response when compared with sheep reared in rural conditions.
sheep maintained under experimental conditions had higher immune response to ET vaccine compared to those maintained under rural conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of the immune response to enterotoxemia vaccine using ELISA in sheep under laboratory and field condition.
the evaluation of immune response in sheep to ET vaccine in experimental and field conditions.
the evaluation of the protective antibody titre against enterotoxaemia in sheep using ELISA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immune response to ET vaccine was found to be higher in sheep reared in experimental conditions than that of those under field conditions.
the ELISA test could be used as a tool in the field conditions for evaluation of immune responses of sheep against ET vaccine.
the immune response of sheep to ET is better under experimental condition than under field conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the ELISA is a useful tool to monitor the protective immunity against ET in sheep.
the ELISA test could be used as a tool for evaluating the immune response of ET vaccinated sheep under experimental and field conditions.
ELISA can be used as an alternative to agar gel immunodiffusion for evaluation of protective antibody titre in sheep vaccinated against ET.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sheep reared under rural conditions have poor immunity and are more prone to ET infection.
the sheep vaccinated with booster dose in farms could maintain protective antibody titre for 4 months and the same was found to be maintained for 3 months in those maintained under field conditions.
the sheep reared under field conditions have low immune response when compared to those reared under experimental/laboratoy conditions.
